hardware.topology: one interpreter hosting the proxy thread and the measuring client; the loaded column adds one busy process per CPU, because a shared runner is the condition the budget has to survive

method.bound: the 100 ms budget is a gate on the observed samples of the machine that ran this file. It is NOT a claim that a rebind is inside 100 ms on any machine: a thread the OS does not schedule cannot be bounded by this or any sleeping-thread design (defect 58)
method.detection: `listener-notice` closes a listener that still has its notice attached (the fast path); `watchdog-tick` removes the notice first, so the tick is the only detector (the backstop)
method.detection_ms: outage_ms - rebind_ms, every sample: what was not the rebind
method.loaded: one busy process per CPU, in separate interpreters
method.noticed_ms: the supervisor's own detection time (lost_cb -> watchdog saw it); defined only when the listener notified, so `noticed_n` may be smaller than `n`
method.outage_ms: from the listener being closed to a new listener serving on the same port: what a child experiences, and the only number the gate is on
method.phase: each trial sleeps a seeded random fraction of a tick before breaking the listener, so the samples cover the whole detection phase instead of locking onto the worst case
